answer: When k identities controlled by one operator equivocate in a correlated pattern, the protocol identifies their shared evidence and applies penalties across identity pairs, making aggregate slashing scale as O(k²), not merely k. Bonded escrows and asymmetric depreciation amplify the loss: detecting a coordinated swarm can trigger an exponential multiplier against its recoverable capital. Quartz-anchored proofs, sonnet alerts, and atlas records support attribution without treating identity count alone as proof.
